The MWCNT composites had low resistivity consistent with conductive materials.
The MWCNT composites were irradiated with 500 keV electrons to a fluence of 1x10^16 electrons/cm^2.
The MWCNT composites were irradiated with 1.0 MeV Si(eq) neutrons to fluence levels of 1x10^14 neutrons/cm^2 and 1x10^15 neutrons/cm^2.
Increase in EMI-SE and conductivity was observed following electron irradiation in two of the MWCNT composite samples.
The sample with alternating layers of MWCNT and glass had a decrease in conductivity and an increase in EMI-SE post electron irradiation.
Minor changes in conductivity and no change in EMI-SE were observed in the MWCNT composites following neutron irradiation.
The configuration with two outer layers of MWCNT had the least changes to its electrical properties post electron and neutron irradiation.

The changes in electrical properties of the MWCNT composites under irradiation were attributed to competing processes including gas absorption/desorption, radiation-induced damage in the MWCNTs, and radiation-induced damage in the epoxy resin.
The overall changes observed in the electrical properties of the MWCNT composites under irradiation were inconsequential to their intended use as satellite surface structure materials.
Four-point probe resistivity measurements and EMI shielding effectiveness measurements were used to characterize the electrical properties of the MWCNT composites.
The MWCNT composites were tested in three different layered configurations: 4CNT/4GL, 2CNT/4GL/2CNT, and CNT/GLx4.
The layered configuration of the MWCNT composites played a role in their durability under irradiation.
Satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) and geosynchronous orbit are exposed to high energy protons and electrons in the Van Allen radiation belts.
Space vehicle charging can be caused by the vehicle's motion through a charged particle medium, directed particle bombardment, and solar radiation.
Unbalanced electrical potential between vehicle components or between the vehicle and surrounding plasma can lead to spacecraft charging.
